results.title: The largest factorial that is a Fibonacci integer is $36!$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the factorial $n!$ lies in the subgroup of the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Q}^\times$ generated by the Fibonacci numbers $F_m$ with $m \ge 1$ if and only if $n \le 36$.

results.title: Carmichael's congruence for primitive prime divisors of Fibonacci numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$-th Fibonacci number. For every natural number $m > 12$, every primitive prime divisor $p$ of $F_m$ (a prime $p$ that divides $F_m$ but divides no $F_n$ with $0 < n < m$) satisfies $p \equiv \pm 1 \pmod{m}$, that is, $p \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$ or $p + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{m}$.

results.title: Entry point in the Fibonacci sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The entry point (rank of apparition) $z(k)$ of a natural number $k$ is the least $m > 0$ such that $k$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_m$, and $z(k) = 0$ if there is no such $m$.

results.title: Fibonacci entry point of $2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The least $m > 0$ such that $2$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_m$ is $3$, that is, the Fibonacci entry point of $2$ is $z(2) = 3$.

results.title: Fibonacci entry point of $5$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The least $m > 0$ such that $5$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_m$ is $5$, that is, the Fibonacci entry point of $5$ is $z(5) = 5$.

results.title: Fibonacci cyclotomic values
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $m$, $\Phi_m$ is the rational number $\prod_{d \mid m} F_{m/d}^{\mu(d)}$, where $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $m$, $F_k$ is the $k$-th Fibonacci number and $\mu$ is the Möbius function. For $m > 1$ this is the value $\Phi_m(\alpha, \beta)$ of the homogenized $m$-th cyclotomic polynomial at the roots $\alpha, \beta$ of $x^2 - x - 1$.

results.title: Fibonacci cyclotomic value at $2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Fibonacci cyclotomic value $\Phi_2 = \prod_{d \mid 2} F_{2/d}^{\mu(d)} = F_2 / F_1$, where $F_k$ is the $k$-th Fibonacci number and $\mu$ is the Möbius function, equals $1$.

results.title: Primitive part of a Fibonacci number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $m$, the primitive part of the Fibonacci number $F_m$ is $\Psi_m = \prod_p p^{a_p}$, where the product runs over the primes $p$ dividing $F_m$ whose Fibonacci entry point is $z(p) = m$, and $a_p$ is the exponent of $p$ in $F_m$.

results.title: Primitive part of $F_6$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The primitive part of the Fibonacci number $F_6$ is $\Psi_6 = 1$: $F_6 = 8 = 2^3$ and the Fibonacci entry point of $2$ is $z(2) = 3 \ne 6$, so $F_6$ has no prime factor $p$ with $z(p) = 6$.

results.title: Bilateral shift of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $x : \mathbb{Z} \to K$ with values in any set $K$, the bilateral (forward) shift of $x$ is the function $Sx : \mathbb{Z} \to K$ given by $(Sx)(n) = x(n - 1)$.

results.title: Bilateral backward shift of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $x : \mathbb{Z} \to K$ with values in any set $K$, the bilateral backward shift of $x$ is the function $Bx : \mathbb{Z} \to K$ given by $(Bx)(n) = x(n + 1)$.

results.title: Bilateral shift as a linear map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of square-summable functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{K}$. The bilateral shift is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $S : \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Sx)(n) = x(n - 1)$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Bilateral backward shift as a linear map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of square-summable functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{K}$. The bilateral backward shift is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $B : \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Bx)(n) = x(n + 1)$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Bilateral shift operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ be the Hilbert space of square-summable functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{K}$. The bilateral shift is the bounded $\mathbb{K}$-linear operator $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Sx)(n) = x(n - 1)$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Bilateral backward shift operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ be the Hilbert space of square-summable functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{K}$. The bilateral backward shift is the bounded $\mathbb{K}$-linear operator $B$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Bx)(n) = x(n + 1)$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: A unit scalar times its conjugate is one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ satisfies $|\mu| = 1$, then $\mu \bar{\mu} = 1$, where $\bar{\mu}$ is the complex conjugate of $\mu$.

results.title: Conjugates of unimodular scalars are nonzero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ satisfies $|\mu| = 1$, then its conjugate $\bar{\mu}$ is nonzero.

results.title: Multiplying a power of the conjugate by a unit scalar
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and write $\bar{\mu}$ for the complex conjugate of $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$. If $|\mu| = 1$, then for every integer $n$, $\mu \bar{\mu}^{\,n} = \bar{\mu}^{\,n-1}$.

results.title: Truncated approximate eigenfunction of the bilateral shift
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$, and write $\bar{\mu}$ for the complex conjugate of $\mu$. This is the function $f_{\mu,N} : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{K}$ with $f_{\mu,N}(n) = \bar{\mu}^{\,n}$ for $-N \le n \le N$ and $f_{\mu,N}(n) = 0$ otherwise (negative powers are inverses, with the convention $0^{n} = 0$ for $n < 0$).

results.title: Truncated approximate eigenvector of the bilateral shift
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$, and write $\bar{\mu}$ for the complex conjugate of $\mu$. This is the vector $v_{\mu,N} \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ whose $n$-th coordinate is the truncated approximate eigenfunction $f_{\mu,N}(n)$, that is, $\bar{\mu}^{\,n}$ for $-N \le n \le N$ and $0$ otherwise; it lies in $\ell^2$ because it has finite…

results.title: Norm of the truncated approximate eigenvector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $|\mu| = 1$, and let $N \in \mathbb{N}$. The truncated approximate eigenvector $v_{\mu,N} \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, whose $n$-th coordinate is $\bar{\mu}^{\,n}$ for $-N \le n \le N$ and $0$ otherwise ($\bar{\mu}$ the complex conjugate of $\mu$), satisfies $\|v_{\mu,N}\|^2 = 2N + 1$.

results.title: Applying $\mu I - T$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$, and let $\mu I$ be the image of $\mu$ under the algebra map from $\mathbb{K}$ to the bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, that is, $\mu$ times the identity. Then for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, $(\mu I - T)x = \mu x - Tx$.

results.title: Coordinates of the residual of the truncated approximate eigenvector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be the bilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$, $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Let $f_{\mu,N}$ be the truncated approximate eigenfunction and $v_{\mu,N} \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ the corresponding truncated approximate eigenvector. Then the $n$-th coordinate of $(\mu I - S)v_{\mu,N}$ is…

results.title: Residual of the truncated approximate eigenvector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be the bilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $|\mu| = 1$, and let $N \in \mathbb{N}$. The truncated approximate eigenvector $v_{\mu,N}$ satisfies $\|(\mu I - S)v_{\mu,N}\|^2 = 2$, where $\mu I$ is $\mu$ times the identity operator.

results.title: Every point of the unit circle lies in the spectrum of the bilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $S$ be the bilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$. Every $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $|\mu| = 1$ lies in the spectrum of $S$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, that is, $\mu I - S$ is not invertible there, where $\mu I$ is $\mu$ times the identity operator.

results.title: Spectrum of the bilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The spectrum of the bilateral shift, as a bounded operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, is the set of scalars $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $|\mu| = 1$; for $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{C}$ this is the unit circle.

results.title: Spectrum of the bilateral backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $B$ be the bilateral backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$. The spectrum of $B$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ is the unit circle $\{\mu \in \mathbb{K} : |\mu| = 1\}$.

results.title: Poisson process
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: `N : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℕ` is a Poisson process of rate `r` under `P` (Kingman 1993, ch. 4; Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4): `N 0 = 0` and the paths are nondecreasing almost surely, the increments over consecutive intervals are independent, and for `s ≤ t` the increment `N t - N s` has the Poisson law of mean `r (t - s)`.

results.title: Arrival times from interarrival times
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `n`-th arrival time `S n = T 0 + ⋯ + T (n - 1)` of the interarrival times `T`.

results.title: Counting process of interarrival times
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The counting process of the interarrival times `T`: `count T t ω` is the number of arrivals `n ≥ 1` with `S n ≤ t`. When that set is infinite (a null event for exponential interarrivals of positive rate) `Set.ncard` returns `0`.

results.title: Arrival times of exponential interarrivals are Erlang
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The `(n + 1)`-th arrival time of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals has the Gamma (Erlang) law with shape `n + 1` and rate `r` (Karlin–Taylor 1975, §4.2).

results.title: Arrival counts of exponential interarrivals are Poisson
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number of arrivals in `[0, t]` of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals has the Poisson law of mean `r t` (Karlin–Taylor 1975, §4.2, Theorem 2.1).

results.title: Counting process starts at zero almost surely
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals starts at `0` almost surely (all interarrival times are positive almost surely).

results.title: Counting process has nondecreasing paths almost surely
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals has nondecreasing paths almost surely (the arrival times tend to infinity almost surely, so every arrival set in `[0, t]` is finite).

results.title: Superposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Superposition (Kingman 1993, §2.2): the sum of two independent Poisson processes of rates `r₁` and `r₂` is a Poisson process of rate `r₁ + r₂`. Independence is of the two processes as random paths.

results.title: Thinning of a Poisson process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The thinning of `N` by the marks `B`: the number of indices `i < N t` with `B i`, i.e. the number of points of `N` in `[0, t]` that are kept when the `i`-th point (in time order, from `0`) is kept iff `B i`.

results.title: Thinning
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Thinning (Kingman 1993, §5.1; Karlin–Taylor 1975, §4.1): keeping each point of a Poisson process of rate `r` independently with probability `p`, independently of the process, gives a Poisson process of rate `p r`. The marks `B i` are i.i.d. with `P(B i) = p` and independent of `N` as a random path.

results.title: Independent Poisson increments of the counting process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The increments of the counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals over consecutive intervals `(t i, t (i + 1)]` are independent with the Poisson laws of means `r (t (i + 1) - t i)`: the increment vector has the product law (Kingman 1993, ch. 4; Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4).

results.title: Exponential interarrivals give a Poisson process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Exponential interarrivals give a Poisson process (Kingman 1993, ch. 4; Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4): the counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrival times is a Poisson process of rate `r`.

results.title: Sum-free sets of natural numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $S$ of natural numbers is sum-free if $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$, where $x = y$ is allowed.

results.title: Green's Problem 1 on large sum-free subsets

results.summary: The statement that there is a function $\omega$ from the natural numbers to the real numbers with $\omega(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ such that every finite set $A$ of positive integers contains a sum-free subset $B \subseteq A$ with $|B| \ge |A|/3 + \omega(|A|)$.

results.title: Bedert's theorem on large sum-free subsets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a function $\omega$ from the natural numbers to the real numbers with $\omega(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ such that every finite set $A$ of positive integers contains a subset $B \subseteq A$ with $x + y \notin B$ for all $x, y \in B$ (a sum-free subset) and $|B| \ge |A|/3 + \omega(|A|)$.

Here $\pi$ contains $312$ if there are $i < j < k$ with $\pi(j) < \pi(k) < \pi(i)$, and contains $231$ if there are $i < j < k$ with $\pi(k) < \pi(i) < \pi(j)$.

results.title: Number of symmetric peaks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_m$ of natural numbers, a symmetric peak is a factor $w_i w_{i+1} w_{i+2}$ of three consecutive letters with $w_i = w_{i+2} < w_{i+1}$. The number of symmetric peaks of $w$ is the number of indices $i$ with $1 \le i \le m - 2$ at which $w$ has a symmetric peak (overlapping peaks all count); it is $0$ when $m < 3$.

results.title: Sum of the heights of symmetric peaks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_m$ of natural numbers, a symmetric peak is a factor $w_i w_{i+1} w_{i+2}$ of three consecutive letters with $w_i = w_{i+2} < w_{i+1}$, and its height is $w_{i+1} - w_i$. The symmetric peak height sum of $w$ is the sum of the heights of the symmetric peaks of $w$ over all indices $i$ with $1 \le i \le m - 2$ at which one occurs; it is $0$ when $m < 3$.

results.title: Number of symmetric valleys of a word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_\ell$ of natural numbers, a symmetric valley is a position $i$ with $1 < i < \ell$ such that $w_{i-1} = w_{i+1}$ and $w_i < w_{i-1}$, that is, a factor $a\,b\,a$ with $b < a$. The symmetric valley count of $w$ is the number of such positions; in particular it is $0$ when $\ell < 3$.

results.title: Total depth of the symmetric valleys of a word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_\ell$ of natural numbers, a symmetric valley is a position $i$ with $1 < i < \ell$ such that $w_{i-1} = w_{i+1}$ and $w_i < w_{i-1}$; its depth is $w_{i-1} - w_i$. The symmetric valley depth sum of $w$ is the sum of the depths of all its symmetric valleys; in particular it is $0$ when $\ell < 3$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The symmetric peak height sums of the words $1\,3\,1$, $1\,2\,1\,1$, $1\,1\,2\,1$ and $1\,1\,1\,1\,1$ are $2$, $1$, $1$ and $0$ respectively, and the word $1\,3\,1$ has exactly one symmetric peak.

results.title: Independent dominating set instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET is a triple $(n, E, K)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edges, and a natural number $K$, the bound on the size of the set.

results.title: Graph of an independent dominating set instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an independent dominating set instance with $n$ vertices and edge list $E$, the graph of the instance is the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ belongs to $E$.

results.title: Well-formed independent dominating set instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An independent dominating set instance $(n, E, K)$ is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(a, b)$ in $E$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$, $a \ne b$, and $(b, a)$ does not belong to $E$.

results.title: Instances with a small independent dominating set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An independent dominating set instance $(n, E, K)$ has a small independent dominating set when there is a set $S$ of vertices of its graph with at most $K$ elements such that every vertex lies in $S$ or is adjacent to a vertex of $S$, and no two distinct vertices of $S$ are adjacent.

results.title: INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an independent dominating set instance $(n, E, K)$ that is well formed and whose graph has an independent dominating set of at most $K$ vertices. It rejects every bitstring that does not decode to an instance.

results.title: INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.

results.title: The encoded index terminal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the index $i$ as an encoded terminal over the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathbb{N}$: the element $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{inr}\, i)$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathbb{N})$, whose left summand $\mathbb{N}$ holds the nonterminals and whose right summand holds the terminals.

results.title: Encoded nonterminal symbol
results.caption: Definition
